1067-scholarships-bursaries-and-prizes: See the Undergraduate Scholarships and Student Aid Calendar, the Graduate Fellowships and Awards Calendar, and Nursing's Funding Opportunities page.
1067-entrance-scholarships: Several are open to all Canadians; see the Calendar. Those below are for Nursing students.
1068-isabel-clarke-dickson-woodrow-schol: Since 2000, for Canadians entering undergraduate Nursing: standing first, then need or leadership. Leftover funds may become bursaries.
1068-woman-s-general-reddy-memorial-and-: Since 2001, after a year of study, preferring working nurses with a college diploma returning for a degree.
1068-gail-carson-travel-award: Since 2015, travel for students on Clinical Internships in underdeveloped communities.
1068-luella-downing-prize-in-nursing: Since 2006, for an undergraduate past first year who contributed to School and class life.
1068-mildred-b-lande-scholarship-in-the-: Since 2008, for top undergraduates past first year: two at $1,500 or one at $3,000.
1068-nursing-alumnae-award: Several, about $1,000 each, for second- and third-years and graduates, including the Marion Lindeburgh, Irma Riley, Agnes Boisde, Montreal General Alumnae and MGH Flo Mackenzie awards. The School applies early in Fall.
1068-the-robert-h-lennox-and-elizabeth-g: Since 2007, one for a B.Sc. student and one for a B.Sc.(N.) student past first year, on high standing, preferring international students.
1068-the-pearson-education-book-prize: Yearly for one top student in each undergraduate year. Ask the School about other Book Prizes and funding.
1068-anne-marie-fong-hum-memorial-prize: Since 1985, for sensitivity and skill helping patients and families with long-term illness.
1068-barbara-ann-altshuler-prize-in-nurs: Since 2006, on clinical and academic achievement.
1068-evelyn-rocque-malowany-prize-in-nur: Since 2007, for a graduate showing initiative and leadership.
1069-lexy-l-fellowes-memorial-prize: Since 1969, for the highest academic and professional achievement in the B.Sc.(N.).
1069-the-pearson-education-book-prize: Yearly for one top student in each undergraduate year.
1069-registration-and-regulations: New students: see mcgill.ca/getready/orientation, and register in Minerva by the August Orientation or pay late fees. To guarantee clinical placement, returning students register by June 15 (Fall), November 15 (Winter) and March 15 (Summer).
1069-degree-evaluation: You must check you meet degree requirements (p. 60).
1069-communication-policy: Email is official. Give your name and McGill ID in messages.
1069-general-course-requirements: Courses open with objectives and grading. Meet requirements, including attendance, to write the exam. Conferences such as Nursing Explorations are expected, with a fee.
1069-leave-of-absence: See p. 24 and the Handbook. Not returning after a year's leave means withdrawing, with readmission possible within a year.
1069-withdrawal: Get the Program Director's permission to drop a required course, and talk to them before leaving the program. Withdrawing from Fall courses counts as leaving McGill unless on leave. If you leave nursing or transfer, return your proof of registration to the OIIQ. See p. 46.
1069-academic-standing-and-evaluation-sy: The Student Standing and Promotions Committee meets at least three times a year. It reviews all students and OIIQ requirements, handles leaves, deferred and supplemental policy, rereads, first appeals, and conduct concerns, and may delegate to Program Directors or the Nursing Student Affairs Office (NSAO).
1069-grading: C passes in B.Sc.(N.) and B.N.(I). See p. 53.
1070-satisfactory-unsatisfactory-s-u-opt: Electives only, one a term, not required or complementary courses. Best for upper-level courses. Most awards need 27 graded credits. Once S/U, no grade can be assigned. See p. 36.
1070-standing-in-undergraduate-nursing-p: Satisfactory for U1–U3: CGPA 2.0+, at most 7 credits failed in non-clinical courses, no failed clinical courses (NUR1 230–236, 331–339, 431–435, 529–531), at most one clinical course at B or below or minimally meeting objectives, and professional behaviour under the Quebec Code of Ethics of Nurses, McGill's Code and the Faculty Code.
U0: CGPA 2.0+ and at most three failures, reset on entering U1. Otherwise the Committee decides, weighing your pattern, circumstances, reason for clinical failure and any code violations.
1070-probationary-standing: When allowed to continue with: CGPA 1.5–1.99 within allowed failures from Satisfactory; at most three U0 failures; or TGPA 2.5+ after Probation. Also an exceptional second weak clinical course, professional lapses with provisions, or readmission.
Maximum 14 credits a term. Keep TGPA 2.5 and reach CGPA 2.0 by the end of next year, plus any Committee conditions. See NSAO.
1070-unsatisfactory-standing: You must withdraw from the program, though you may be fine elsewhere at McGill; see NSAO.

Triggers: CGPA under 1.5; too many failures without permission; after Probation, TGPA under 2.5 with CGPA under 2.0 or unmet conditions; failed clinical without a repeat; unprofessional conduct or code violations without permission to continue; unsuitability for nursing; OIIQ license revoked; or no clinical access because of a criminal offence.
1071-interim-standings: After one term below Satisfactory. Continue, at 14 credits at most, with your advisor's review.
1071-clinical-support: Supports learning and patient safety; on your School file, not Minerva. Triggered by B to C or minimal performance in a clinical course, professionalism concerns, two or more terms away from clinical work, or a permitted clinical repeat.
Continue under a learning plan with coordinators; not progressing means an F. Only one in your program, apart from absence notices.
1071-appeals: Only decisions of Unsatisfactory or required withdrawal. Write to the Committee within 14 days with reasons and documents. Further appeals go to the Associate Dean and Director. See the Handbook.
1071-readmission-unsatisfactory-readmit: Apply one year after leaving, in Minerva, or to NSAO if still at McGill, with a compelling letter and documents. It depends on resolving the causes, your capacity and seats, and you get one request. Courses on weak areas are recommended. You may have to restart nursing after poor results or a gap over a year. Applying within a year of withdrawal gets priority.
1072-examinations: University rules apply; see p. 62 and the Handbook.
1072-supplemental-examinations: For D, J, F or U with CGPA 2.0+ and Satisfactory Standing; apply in Minerva, NSAO decides. None after a deferred exam: re-register or substitute. At most two in the program, except specially.
Worth the original exam's weight or 100%, and may differ, so ask. Both grades count in your CGPA, and a failed supplemental counts as a failure. If you can't write it, repeat the course.
1072-deferred-examinations: Missed midterms for illness, crisis or religious observance: the instructor may reschedule, set alternative work, shift the weight, or give an alternate final.

Missed finals: apply in Minerva with documents by January 15 (Fall), May 15 (Winter) or July 15 (Summer). Summer courses like CHEM 212 have none. NSAO decides; you see an L. Free, written at the next chance: reading week for Fall, mid-August for Winter. If you can't, contact NSAO for WL; otherwise you get J, counted as zero.
1072-reassessments-and-rereads: You can see and discuss marked work and get an impartial review. Evaluation details come in the first two weeks.

Reassessment: free, through NSAO, within 10 working days; a reviewer checks fairness, not regrades. Reread: written, for a fee; the grade can rise, fall or stay. Deadlines: March 31 (Fall), July 31 (Winter), August 31 (May). Computer-marked exams can only be reassessed.
One course a term. Not for supplementals or clinical courses, where you talk with your teacher and coordinator, with no formal appeal. Other faculties' rules apply to their courses.
1073-procedures-governing-reassessment-r: Reassessment is free; final exam and paper rereads cost a fee. Computer-marked exams can't be reread.
1073-time-to-degree-completion: B.Sc.(N.) from U1: three years with summers, four at most. From U0: four, five at most. B.N.I.: two full-time or three part-time, four at most. Changes need the Program Director's approval and documented reasons.
1073-leave-of-absence-loa: For maternity or parenting, health, or professional or military service, term by term, up to 52 weeks, through NSAO with documents. No tuition; you keep your ID, mail and libraries. Not for travel or money. Usually needs Satisfactory Standing.

Student Services can be opted into. Scholarships pause but stay renewable. Check loan rules with Student Aid; international students see ISS. Not returning after a year means withdrawing, with possible restart.
Return your certificate to the OIIQ on any interruption; it's returned free within a year. After that, register again with documents and fee.
1073-pregnancy-and-nursing-clinical-stud: Contact the Clinical Partnership Office. Some settings are excluded, such as OR, emergency, ICU, post-anesthesia, pediatrics and some psychiatric agencies. Follow your care provider; suitable placement isn't guaranteed, and graduation may be delayed.
1073-clinical-studies-portal-document-up: B.Sc.(N.) and B.N.(I) students must also meet the following.
1073-oiiq-registration: All students need an OIIQ license. See p. 33.
1073-faculty-of-medicine-and-health-scie: Everyone must read it. Deadlines are on the clinical student portal.
1074-vaccination-immunization-requiremen: See p. 24. Yearly flu shots are mandatory. Complete immunizations (Hepatitis B in progress is fine) by your first clinical year: U1 for B.Sc.(N.), U2 for B.N.I., or you can't enter teaching hospitals.
1074-mask-fitting-requirements: Before NUR1 331 or 434, through Student Health Services, valid two years. If a mask can't fit, tell your instructor.
1074-cpr: Keep CPR Health Care Provider certification throughout. The School often runs sessions.
1074-safetalk: A mandatory half-day suicide alertness course for B.Sc.(N.) U1 and B.N.I. U2. Proof required; exemptions with prior certification or experience.
1074-hsp-net-authorization: The BC-run Health Sciences Placement Network coordinates placements. You must authorize use and disclosure of your name and profile, and use of your health information, for placements.
1074-co-op-work-permit-international-stu: Practical work is mandatory, so non-citizens and non-residents need a co-op work permit as well as a study permit, paid or not, before clinical work. Apply with your admission letter, the program's co-op letter, an international student letter and a medical exam. See International Student Services.
1074-criminal-background-verification: Agencies need a self-declaration or formal check; no access means you can't meet course requirements. The OIIQ needs offences declared, and must be told of accusations during studies. Without a student license you can't continue.
1074-clinical-courses: Professional behaviour is expected always under the OIIQ Code, Faculty Code and McGill Code, with mandatory professionalism and interprofessional seminars. Register with the OIIQ first. Identify yourself as a McGill Nursing Student in charts, wear the badge (charged to your account), and follow uniform rules.

Attendance is mandatory; repeat absences may defer your clinical work. If below expectations you make a learning plan; if unsafe you leave the course with an F and meet the Program Director. Buy a stethoscope and equipment, and budget for travel. Expect days, evenings, nights and weekends.

Placements aren't by student choice, except NUR1 435, 530 and 531, and if you or close family work there, you've been a patient there, or SERTIH has limits. Blood-borne infections must be reported to your Program Director and go to SERTIH.

Outside the McGill network (NUR1 435, 531 only): Satisfactory Standing and CGPA 3.2+, some higher, judged on proposal, autonomy, progress and interviews. B.N.(I) students finish all U2 Fall and Winter courses before NUR1 434 or 435.
1075-inter-university-transfer-iut-agree: 3, or exceptionally 6, credits at another Quebec university while paying McGill, in Satisfactory Standing, through BCI. Follow the host's rules. C or better counts as pass, with no GPA effect; failures show as failures. Required courses must be equivalent. See p. 39.
1075-study-away: For courses outside Quebec, in Satisfactory Standing, usually U0's CHEM 212 at home, or an equivalent elective or required course. C minimum.

Steps: confirm it's outside Quebec; check the Course Equivalency System or request assessment; confirm the course runs and you qualify; avoid your graduating term. Apply in Minerva, and register at McGill too as a backup, dropping it later if all goes well.
Then register at the host, have the official transcript sent to NSAO whatever the grade, and check Minerva. Cancel in Minerva if you change your mind.
1076-registration-with-the-profession-im: Quebec law requires it ("immatriculation"), through the OIIQ. Patient access needs a Student Permit (B.Sc.(N.) and nurse practitioner students) or registered nurse status (B.N.I. after the exam).

B.N.I. students who pass must pay OIIQ fees, pro-rated then yearly, with no waiver, or they can't be in clinical settings. Carry proof in all clinical work, since patients, teachers and agents can ask.

You may do nurses' activities needed for your program, except adjusting the therapeutic nursing plan, supervised by a nurse who is present (O.C. 551-2010). Chart with your signature followed by "student n.", printing your name if unclear.

The OIIQ may revoke it after over a year out of the program, if you fail or are expelled, obtained it falsely, or act beyond what's allowed or against ethics. Interrupting suspends it; over a year revokes it.
1077-requirements-for-licensure-entry-in: OIIQ: 4200 Rue Molson, H1Y 4V4. It runs the professional exam. If you finished English high school before 1986, you pass the French Proficiency exam (OQLF, Charter article 35), available in your last two years. Not needed with a Quebec diploma after 1986 or three full-time years in French.

The OIIQ exam is approved under Canada's Mutual Recognition Agreement, so taking it helps; agreements change. Elsewhere, you're generally licensed where you trained first, may write more exams, and should contact the regulator early, especially international students.
1078-undergraduate-programs: B.N.I.: for DEC 180.A.0 holders, within three years of the DEC, on campus or online. B.Sc.(N.): for CEGEP Health or Natural Sciences or equivalent, for entry to practice.
1078-bachelor-of-science-nursing-b-sc-n-: Three years, or four with U0 sciences for high school graduates and mature students without science. Summer sessions included. Clinical work in community centres, hospitals, agencies and homes.
1078-bachelor-of-nursing-b-n-i-integrate: Part of a five-year Quebec plan, for 180.A.0 and 180.A.1 graduates, with 27 credits of Advanced Standing. Two university years, or three part-time, on advanced nursing and science, teamwork or autonomous practice with individuals, families and groups, health education and research. Online suits independent learners.
1078-minor-degrees: From units like Women's Studies or Psychology, generally 18–24 credits, most suited to transfers. Submit the form to NSAO; it's in the Handbook.
1078-program-accreditation: Both are fully accredited by the Canadian Association of Schools of Nursing.
1078-graduate-programs: M.Sc.A. concentrations: Advanced Clinical Practice, Direct Entry Nursing, Global Health, Global Health Direct Entry, and Mental Health, Neonatology, Pediatrics and Primary Care Nurse Practitioner, and Nursing Services Administration. Nurses with bachelor's degrees take the non-direct-entry ones. B.A. or B.Sc. graduates without nursing take Direct Entry, unique in Canada.

Certificates: Theory in Neonatology, Theory in Primary Care. Diplomas: Mental Health, Neonatal, Pediatrics and Primary Care Nurse Practitioner. For licensed nurses with a bachelor's and two years' experience in the field.
Ph.D. for researchers, academics and leaders, requiring master's study and a nursing degree.
1079-quebec-diploma-of-collegial-studies: For the 103-credit program: Biology NYA, General Biology II (00UK, 00XU); Chemistry NYA, NYB, Organic I (00UL, 00UM, 00XV); Math NYA, NYB (00UN, 00UP); Physics NYA, NYB, NYC (00UR, 00US, 00UT). Based on overall and prerequisite Cote R.
1079-mature-students: Age 23+, Canadian or Permanent Resident, with functions (calculus preferred) and two of biology, chemistry or physics with labs, at CEGEP or university, 70% or equivalent. See CEGEP advisors. Admits you to the 136-credit, four-year program, with no repeat of equivalent courses.
1079-applicants-from-ontario: OSSD; usually the four-year program. MCV4U, two of SBI4U, SCH4U or SPH4U, and 4U English or French. Based on "Top 6" 4U and 4M courses, at least four 4U, and all prerequisites at 4U. All grades count. Most applied courses are excluded; up to two 4M arts are allowed.
1079-applicants-from-canadian-high-schoo: A university-access diploma; usually four years. Grade 12 precalculus, two of Biology, Chemistry or Physics, and English or French. Based on "Top 5" Grade 12 courses, with all grades counted.
1079-applicants-from-other-universities-: Judged on pre-university and university work; 60 credits at McGill. Needs two calculus terms, two biology, two general chemistry, one organic, and two physics, with labs. At minimum, two calculus plus two of biology, chemistry or physics, finishing the rest in the program. Past degrees may give equivalence, especially Physiology and Pharmacology. Science and math must be within five years.
1079-applicants-from-the-u-s-high-school: A college-track diploma with precalculus and two of Biology, Chemistry or Physics. SAT IIs in two of Biology, Chemistry, Math or Physics. Grades 10–12 count, especially relevant ones.
1080-applicants-from-outside-canada-or-t: Strong senior math and science; usually four years. Proof of English may be needed: TOEFL 233 (577 paper) or others. See mcgill.ca/applying/requirements.
1080-inter-faculty-transfer-students-mcg: Apply in Minerva. Satisfactory Standing and normally CGPA 2.70, 3.0 preferred.
1080-holders-of-a-bachelor-s-degree: With a general Science or Arts degree by August 1, ask Service Point or the Welcome Centre. You may apply to the B.Sc.(N.) through Enrolment Services, or the Master's Qualifying Year through the School.
1080-b-n-integrated-entrance-requirement: DEC 180A.0 and 180A.1, within three years, based on overall and prerequisite Cote R. Follow the course sequence unless your advisor agrees.
1080-application-procedures: McGill's online application, with two program choices and a non-refundable fee, no waivers.
1080-application-deadlines: Fall: January 15 from outside Canada; February 1 from other Canadian schools and Quebec B.Sc.(N.) applicants; March 1 otherwise, including B.N.I. Winter, if open: November 1. No Summer. Special, Exchange and Visiting match Canadian or International dates.
1080-program-description: 3–4 years with summers, on contemporary nursing issues, core skills and critical thinking. Qualifies you for licensing exams in Quebec, Canada and elsewhere. CASN accredited.
